looksRight: The side street, in every crossing shot from crossing-red (114.71) to cross (165.29), and in the start of the last block (167.71, 170.29): the street ends in one plain building, and below the roofs it is black. No skyline line shows through the street, its road or its gaps. Larger crops at 116.03 and 170.29 confirm it. The only far city is above the roofs, as over any roof. The DON'T WALK and WALK signs are unobstructed.
No other gap in the building fronts shows anything far through it, from crossing-red to last-block. Snow is still flakes, and none covers a face or a sign.

Nothing on the table moves by itself. At served (218.8 to 219.6) the bowl stands still at Larry's left, by Dee's place, and his head is turned to it. After the cut (about 219.85) it is still at our plate and he looks down at it. The two positions read as one bowl that went past him. The table region holds still across the-meal (226.5 to 229.5) and goodnight. The only change between frames is the steam and the caption.
Depth: no glass, candle, plate, bowl or the dish is drawn through another in any table frame, from table-wide (202.2) to the fade.

Sibyl is at the right end of the far side in an open wooden chair in every view: table-wide, sibyl-first, they-look, rule, served and larry-and-sibyl. Her size matches her distance. She is at her plate, chin down, through 'It's my house.' (220.6 to 221.9), and lifts her head and looks level at Larry for 'It's still the rule.' (222.72).

Six stay six in the same seats in every table shot (Pete, Hy, Dee, Al, Eppy and Sibyl, seen from the door). Seven heads appear only in table-wide and they-look. Elsewhere there are four or fewer, and goodnight has no head behind Larry's.
No light change at they-look or goodnight, no glass raised, Pete's hood clear of his mouth, and the scarf and cardigan continuous. The last frame (249.62) is fully black (RGB maximum 0).
forTheOwner: The second chair at chair-in, and the plate and fork that slide in along the bottom of the frame as we sit (seen arriving at 215.0 and settled by 215.6), are now the only things in the special that move by themselves on the table. They are as the script asks, and nothing in the picture is wrong. But now that the bowls no longer slide, the place setting's slide may read as out of keeping. The second chair is in the door view and reads as being pulled up for us. Whether either should arrive after a cut instead is yours to say.
As before: whether the listen holds are heard as us speaking, and whether the coin lands as the tune's missing note. Only sound can settle these.
